issues.legal_issue: A fatal stabbing inflicted after an attack with a stick, in the exercise but excessive use of private defence, is culpable homicide under the first part of Section 304 rather than murder.
material_facts: The accused was struck several times with a stick by the deceased before stabbing him with a knife.
The knife wound pierced the deceased’s heart and was fatal.
The court found that the accused acted in private defence but exceeded that right by stabbing the deceased in the heart.
The accused had been convicted of murder, and the appeal was confined to the nature of the offence and the sentence.
issues.conclusion: The murder conviction was altered to a conviction under the first part of Section 304 of the Indian Penal Code. The court imposed rigorous imprisonment for five years and a fine of Rs. 2,500, with a further two years’ rigorous imprisonment in default of payment.
issues.legal_principle: Applying Sections 302 and 304, first part, of the Indian Penal Code, the court held that the accused’s act was committed in the exercise of private defence, but that he exceeded that right in responding to the attack with a fatal knife blow. The court therefore treated the offence as falling under the first part of Section 304 rather than Section 302. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_on_offence_classification and deceased_attacked_accused_first and accused_inflicted_fatal_stab and accused_exceeded_private_defence

predicates.criminal_appeal_on_offence_classificatio: The proceeding was an appeal in which the classification of a homicide offence was in issue.
predicates.deceased_attacked_accused_first: The deceased struck the accused with a stick before the accused used the knife.
predicates.accused_inflicted_fatal_stab: The accused stabbed the deceased, and the stab caused a fatal wound.
predicates.accused_exceeded_private_defence: The accused acted to defend himself but used force that exceeded the attack he faced.

issues.definition: When the proceeding concerns classification of a homicide offence and the deceased attacked first, the accused inflicted the fatal stab, and the accused exceeded private defence, the offence is treated as culpable homicide rather than murder.

issues.legal_issue: The sentence for an attempted murder conviction may be reduced in light of the circumstances of the case.
material_facts: The accused’s conviction for attempting to murder another person was maintained.
The High Court had imposed a seven-year term of imprisonment for that offence.
The court considered the circumstances of the case to warrant a reduction in that sentence.
issues.conclusion: The sentence for the attempted murder conviction was reduced to five years’ imprisonment, to run concurrently with the sentence for the other offence.
issues.legal_principle: In considering the sentence for the offence under Section 307 of the Indian Penal Code, the court relied on the circumstances of the case as warranting a reduction. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.criminal_appeal_on_sentence: The proceeding was an appeal in which the sentence for a criminal conviction was under review.
predicates.attempted_murder_conviction_upheld: The conviction for attempting to murder another person remained in force.
predicates.case_circumstances_warrant_reduction: The court found the circumstances of the case to support reducing the sentence.

issues.definition: When a sentence is under review on appeal, the attempted murder conviction remains in force, and the court finds that the circumstances warrant a reduction, the sentence for that offence is reduced.
